author: K. P. Poonacha, Bangalore Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Banavasi (Uttara Kannada), fortified township NW of the Madhukeshvara temple
evidence: Trial trench 1994-95 inside the fortification: nine layers, four periods: Chutu (lead/potin coins, punch-marked coin), Satavahana (enclosure wall, mint?, bullae with Roman emperors), Kadamba, post-Kadamba
quote: 24. EXCAVATION AT BANAVASI, DISTRICT UTTARA KANNADA — A trial-trench (5 m square) was laid by K.P. Poonacha … four major periods viz., Period I: Chutu, represented by layers 9 and 8; Period II: Satavahana, marked by layers 7, 6 and 5; Period III: Kadamba
note: First stratified sequence inside Banavasi: a fortified town continuously occupied through the Kadamba period (4th-6th c.) into post-Kadamba times, so a living town in the 7th c. Supports Banavasi as a candidate capital of Konkanapura (11.02; study open: Annagundi (Mizutani) or Banavasi). No Buddhist find this season; no mention of Xuanzang.
Exploration in Anantapur district (a village Ratnagiri in Andhra); false match.

author: K. P. Poonacha, Bangalore Circle, ASI
asr_identification: Banavasi (Uttara Kannada) = a town visited by Hiuen Tsang, with stupas N of the township
evidence: 1995-96 trenches inside the fortified township: Chutu-Satavahana-Kadamba-post-Kadamba sequence reaffirmed; Kadamba box-headed inscription fragment; in Satavahana levels terracotta Hariti, face of Buddha and Bodhisattva with chaitya in the crown (first stratified Buddhist finds at Banavasi); trader's seals; pre-Christian Brahmi on a soapstone casket sherd
quote: continued the trial-excavation in two sectors inside the fortified township of Banavasi … face of Buddha and a Bodhisattva with a chaitya in the crown (pl.XIA), establishing for the first time the Buddhist antiquity of Banavasi in a stratigraphic context. It is to be noted that Hiuen Tsang had visited Banavasi (ancient Vaijayanti) and had noticed many stupas towards the north of the township.
note: Asserts Banavasi as a city Xuanzang visited (as IAR 1970-71 and later, coded at 266, 543), now with stratified Buddhist terracottas; but these are Satavahana-period, not 7th-c., and nothing names Konkanapura. The stupas N of the town are taken from the Xiyu ji (Konkanapura capital), not found. Against Mizutani's Annagundi (11.02, disputed); the study keeps the capital open (Annagundi or Banavasi); this strengthens the Banavasi alternative without settling it.
Excavation at Tiruverkadu; storage-jars compared with Kanchipuram.

Conservation (Bharhut, Udaigiri caves Vidisha, Bijamandal).
Plate captions (Banavasi brick wall, head of Bodhisattva, seals); text coded at 987.

author: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh
name_in_asr: Dantapuram, the ancient capital city of Kalinga

evidence: Excavation 2000-01: Mound I brick structure on dressed-stone foundation with stucco; Mound II medieval stone temple over an early historic brick structure with beads, terracottas, red, black-and-red and tan wares; dated 2nd c. BC-4th c. AD
quote: carried out excavation at Dantapuram - the ancient capital city of Kalinga which lies on the left bank of the River Vamsadhara, 6 km away from Amudalavalasa in Srikakulam district. The mud fort covers an area of 500 acres of land. … Based on these finds the site could be dated from the second century BC to the fourth century AD.
note: Dantapura is a further candidate for the Kalinga capital (10.11, study open: Kalingapatnam/Salihundam or Mukhalingam; Mizutani lists Rajamahendri, Kalingapatam, Mukhalingam, Srikakulam). The excavated early historic town ends in the 4th c. AD, apart from a medieval temple: no 7th-c. occupation shown, so it does not support Dantapura as the capital Xuanzang saw. Not linked to Xuanzang in the report.
